name: Anonymous (Middle High German)
credit: First page of the Nibelungenlied, Manuscript C (Donaueschingen, 13th century) - a manuscript leaf, not a portrait of any poet. Public domain (Wikimedia Commons).
bio: The Nibelungenlied, the great Middle High German heroic epic, is anonymous. It was composed in the Danube region, probably in Austria, around 1200, and survives in several dozen manuscripts and fragments, of which the chief are Manuscripts A, B and C, copied in the 13th century. Its author drew on older Germanic legends of Siegfried and of the fall of the Burgundians, and set them in the courtly world of the Hohenstaufen age.

The poem is written in four-line stanzas of long lines, each divided by a mid-line pause (the caesura), and tells in thirty-nine "adventures" how Siegfried wins Kriemhild, is murdered through Hagen's treachery, and how Kriemhild, now married to Etzel, king of the Huns, brings about the destruction of the Burgundians. It is the national epic of the German-speaking world and a source for Wagner's Ring cycle.

poems.title: Summer and his Pleasures
poems.author: Anonymous (Middle High German)
poems.text:
"Nought I deem so worthy, nought I hold above
The fair bright roses and the love of him I love.
The little birds sing sweet;
They sing in the forest; that glads men's hearts to hear.
But if my lover comes not, the summer brings me little cheer."

poems.title: Reward of Service
poems.author: Anonymous (Middle High German)
poems.text:
"A knight there is," a lady said,
"Hath served me as I wished full fain.
Or ere the time of year be fled,
His due reward he needs must gain.
Now snow and winter seem to me
Flowers and clover fair to be,
When in my arms I hold him fast
Though all the world should take it ill
Yet must he get his will at last!"

poems.title: A Merry Heart
poems.author: Anonymous (Middle High German)
poems.text:
The forest stands all green to see;
Oh, the joyous time of year!
Now from sorrows I am free;
Blessings on the maiden dear
Who doth fairly ease my woe!
I am glad; she will have it so.

She beckoned me and gave a glance,
When on her last I set mine eyes.
Thereafter nothing else could chance
Save that she spoke in loving wise:
"Dear, now let thy heart be high!"
How joyous at that speech am I!

"Thou wilt make me weep anon,"
Said the best of maidens there.—
Thou wilt bid me welcome soon
And wilt give me comfort fair.
As thou wilt, so will I be.
Dearest maiden, laugh with me!

poems.title: The Nightingale
poems.author: Anonymous (Middle High German)
poems.text:
So sweetly sang the nightingale,
That we should thank her without fail
And other little birds, I ween.
I thought upon my lady then,—
My lady, who is my heart's queen.

poems.title: Summer
poems.author: Anonymous (Middle High German)
poems.text:
Now grim winter hath left us free.
The summer-tide is lovely to see.
Heath and forest show to me
Clover, flowers, and leaves on the tree.
Never again can our mirth now flee!

poems.title: Dû bist mîn, ich bin dîn
poems.author: Anonymous (Middle High German)
poems.text:
Dû bist mîn, ich bin dîn.
des solt dû gewis sîn.
dû bist beslozzen
in mînem herzen,
verlorn ist das sluzzelîn:
dû muost ouch immêr darinne sîn.
